title: What Blood Is Made Of
objective: After this level you can name the parts of blood and what each one does.
summary: Blood is over half plasma, a watery liquid, plus red cells (about 45 percent) that carry oxygen on hemoglobin, and a sliver of white cells and platelets. Adults have about 4 to 6 liters.

cards.headline: Spin a tube of blood and it splits into layers.
cards.body: Put a blood sample in a centrifuge and it separates: plasma on top, a thin pale layer in the middle, red cells at the bottom. Blood is plasma plus red cells, white cells and platelets. So what is each layer doing?

cards.fact: Over half your blood is plasma, and plasma is about 92% water.
cards.context: It's a watery liquid with salts and proteins dissolved in it, and everything else in blood rides along in it. An adult has about 4 to 6 liters of blood in all. Remember Level 7's water outside your cells? Part of that third is right here, flowing.

cards.headline: Red cells: the oxygen couriers
cards.body: Red blood cells make up about 45 percent of blood's volume, and Level 3 found they are about 84 percent of all your cells. Their job is delivering oxygen from your lungs to your tissues. The carrier is hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that also gives blood its color. Fresh from the lungs, blood is bright red; after dropping off oxygen, it's a duskier red. Never blue.

mascot.line: Bright red or dusky red, but never blue. Blood only comes in shades of red.

cards.headline: The thin pale band
cards.body: That middle layer holds the rest: white blood cells, which fight infection, and platelets, which help blood clot when you cut yourself. Together they're less than 1 percent of a blood sample. The smallest share of blood, doing two of its most urgent jobs. Platelets get their moment in Level 28.

Red cells, about 45%, carry oxygen on hemoglobin
Bright red with oxygen, dusky red without

questions.prompt: Which part of blood makes up more than half of its volume?
questions.explanation: Plasma, a liquid that is about 92 percent water, makes up over half of blood.

questions.prompt: Blood fresh from the lungs is bright red; blood coming back from the tissues is a duskier red. Why?

options.label: It has turned blue inside the veins
options.rationale: Blood is never blue; it stays red.

options.label: It has given up oxygen to the tissues
It has picked up extra platelets

questions.explanation: Hemoglobin changes color with oxygen: bright red when loaded, dusky red after dropping oxygen off.

questions.prompt: Level 3 found red blood cells are your most numerous cells. What is their job?

options.label: Fighting infection
options.rationale: That is the white blood cells' job.

options.label: Carrying salts in the plasma
options.rationale: Salts are dissolved in the plasma itself.

questions.explanation: Red blood cells deliver oxygen from the lungs to the tissues, carried by hemoglobin.
